title: Assembly: Reading Machine Code
subtitle: What your program actually became
audience: For anyone who can write C and now wants to see what the compiler produced — and for anyone heading toward reverse engineering, exploit analysis or low-level debugging, where the source is not available and the binary is the only evidence.
outcomes: Read x86-64 disassembly and follow what it does, instruction by instruction
Name the registers, their widths, and which ones survive a function call
Recognise compiler transformations: division by multiplication, loops replaced by arithmetic, lea used as maths
Trace control flow through comparisons, conditional jumps and loops
Follow the stack through a call, a frame and a recursive descent
Use objdump and a debugger to examine a binary you did not build
